title: An algebraic monogenic extension of a Nagata domain is Japanese
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be integral domains, with an injective algebra map $A\to B$. Assume $A$ is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. Let $x\in B$ generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra and be algebraic over $A$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]: it satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $A$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $B$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] with respect to its fraction field.

proof.text: Let A -> B be an injective monogenic extension of domains with generator x algebraic over A. Embed K = Frac(A) in L = Frac(B). The nonzero polynomial relation over A stays nonzero over K, so x is algebraic over K. The field K(x) contains B and therefore all its fractions, so equals L; finite generation by algebraic elements gives L/K finite. For any finite M/L the tower law gives M/K finite. A is N-2 by the Nagata-domain lemma. Its integral closure A' in M is therefore finite over A, normal with fraction field M, and Nagata by finiteness over a Nagata ring.

*Algebraic case of (*): $S'$ is the integral closure of $T=R'[x]$.* Let $T\subseteq M$ be the subring generated by $R'$ and $x$ (note $x\in B\subseteq L\subseteq M$). Every element of $T$ is a sum $\sum_i\rho_ix^i$ with $\rho_i\in R'$, and writing $\rho_i=\sum_j a_{ij}r_j$ with $a_{ij}\in A$ gives $\sum_i\rho_ix^i=\sum_j(\sum_i a_{ij}x^i)r_j$ with $\sum_ia_{ij}x^i\in B$; so $T$ is the $B$-module generated by $r_1,\dots,r_k$, a finitely generated $B$-module. Its field of fractions is $M$: $R'\subseteq T\subseteq M$ and every element of $M$ is a quotient of elements of $R'$ (step 2). Every element of $R'$ is integral over $A\subseteq B$, hence over $B$ (the same monic equation), so the integral closure $S'$ of $B$ in $M$, a subring of $M$ containing $B$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], contains $R'$ and $x$, hence $T$: $T\subseteq S'$ and $T$ is integral over $B$. Let $T'$ be the integral closure of $T$ in $M$. An element of $S'$ is integral over $B\subseteq T$, hence over $T$: $S'\subseteq T'$. Conversely $T'$ is integral over $T$ and $T$ is integral over $B$, so $T'$ is integral over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]: $T'\subseteq S'$. Hence $S'=T'$.

proof.text: Apply the normal-Nagata monogenic N-1 lemma to A', its fraction field M, and the image of x. Thus T = A'[x] is N-1. Its integral closure T' in M is finite over T. The preceding step identifies T' with the integral closure of B in M and makes T finite over B. Transitivity of module finiteness makes this closure finite over B. Since M/L was arbitrary, B is N-2.
